# Kitebaze site reference

> Expanded, text-first reference for the canonical public pages on kitebaze.com.

Publisher: Kitebaze
Website: https://kitebaze.com/
Language: en-CA
Contact: support@kitebaze.com

This file summarizes public website content for retrieval and citation. Where a case study reports a result, it is identified as a page-reported outcome. Technical crawler preferences are published in robots.txt; access, automated collection, and reuse remain subject to the Terms of Use.

## Home

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/

Kitebaze designs and maintains practical AI and workflow automation around the tools your team already uses, so repetitive work keeps moving.

Kitebaze finds the repetitive work slowing a business down, redesigns the workflow around the software already in use, and builds the automation that keeps the work moving.

The work is practical and operator-led: connect existing tools, remove manual handoffs, preserve human review where judgment matters, and keep improving the system after launch.

## About Kitebaze

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/about-us

Meet the operators behind Kitebaze and learn how we design practical AI and workflow systems that hold up in real businesses.

Kitebaze is operator-led. The company maps how work actually moves before choosing tools or automations, then builds systems designed to hold up outside a demo.

Kitebaze was co-founded by Jason Katz and Leigh Buckley. Their work connects operations, technology, people, and implementation.

## Case Studies

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/case-studies

See how Kitebaze improved billing, case management, field documentation and patient flow with practical workflow automation.

The case studies cover IT-service billing and installation tracking, estate and probate case management, driver-document intake and dispatch, and patient waiting-room flow.

Page-reported outcomes include faster month-end invoice preparation, less manual email entry, cleaner case visibility, centralized driver communications, and improved staff utilization.

## Workflow Build

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/workflow-build

Redesign connected workflows, handoffs, controls and visibility so work moves reliably across your business.

Workflow Build is for work that crosses multiple people, teams, or systems and cannot be improved by fixing one isolated task.

The engagement can include an operating blueprint, connected workflows, clear handoffs, built-in checks, live visibility, documentation, training, and staged rollout.

## Fix One Bottleneck

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/bottleneck

Map one recurring workflow end to end and remove the repetitive copying, checking, chasing and follow-up.

Bottleneck is a focused starting point for one recurring job that is delayed, dropped, or dependent on someone copying, checking, chasing, or reminding.

Kitebaze maps the workflow, finds the friction, defines the guardrails and success measure, then removes repetitive steps and proves the result before expanding.

## Book a Workflow Review

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/book-workflow-review

Book a free 30-minute review to identify manual bottlenecks, automation opportunities and the best first build.

The free 30-minute workflow review is a no-obligation Google Meet focused on one real workflow.

The conversation covers how the work runs today, recurring bottlenecks, practical automation opportunities, and whether one bottleneck or a broader Workflow Build is the right place to begin.

## Free Workflow Diagnostic

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/diagnostics

Describe a manual task and get a free diagnostic showing where automation could remove bottlenecks and repetitive work.

The interactive workflow diagnostic asks a few follow-up questions about a repetitive task and helps identify what could run without constant manual intervention.

## Contact Kitebaze

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/contact

Tell Kitebaze where work is getting stuck, share your workflow challenge or book a free workflow review.

Use the contact form to describe a workflow challenge, or book a free Workflow Review for a live conversation.

Kitebaze lists a Calgary, Alberta, Canada contact address. General enquiries can be sent to support@kitebaze.com.

## Responsible Automation

Canonical URL: https://kitebaze.com/responsible-automation

Explore the seven principles Kitebaze uses to design trustworthy workflows, automations and connected systems.

Kitebaze uses seven principles when designing and deploying systems: Human Control, Security, Privacy, Reliability, Transparency, Accountability, and AI Use.

The technology follows the problem. Automation should remove unnecessary work while keeping people involved where judgment, approval, or escalation matters.

## Full public legal text

### Privacy Policy

**Last updated: September 24, 2026**

Kitebaze (“Kitebaze,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) helps businesses improve how work gets done by redesigning workflows, connecting existing tools, automating repetitive tasks, and supporting the systems we build.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, store, and protect personal information when you:

* visit **kitebaze.com**;
* contact us or book a consultation;
* become a Kitebaze client;
* communicate with us;
* use a workflow, automation, form, assistant, integration, or other solution we configure or operate; or
* otherwise interact with our services.

Because Kitebaze often works with systems and information belonging to our clients, our role can vary.

For information we collect directly for our own business purposes, such as website inquiries, client contacts, and billing information, Kitebaze is responsible for that information.

When we process information through a system or workflow on behalf of a client, the client generally determines why that information is being used and Kitebaze processes it to provide the agreed service.

#### 1. Information We Collect

##### Information you provide directly

We may collect information you choose to give us, including:

* your name;
* email address;
* telephone number;
* company name;
* job title or role;
* information submitted through forms;
* consultation or project details;
* support requests;
* billing and transaction information; and
* information contained in emails, messages, documents, meetings, or other communications with us.

We only ask for information that is reasonably necessary for the interaction or service.

##### Website and technical information

When you visit our website, certain information may be collected automatically, including:

* IP address;
* browser and device information;
* operating system;
* pages visited;
* referring pages or websites;
* approximate location derived from technical information;
* dates and times of visits; and
* interactions with our website.

We may use cookies, analytics tools, and similar technologies to understand how our website is being used and to improve it.

#### 2. Information We Process While Working With Clients

Kitebaze builds around the systems and processes a business already uses.

Depending on the engagement, this can mean working with information contained in:

* email and inboxes;
* spreadsheets;
* CRM systems;
* accounting or invoicing software;
* calendars;
* forms;
* customer-support systems;
* messaging platforms;
* project-management systems;
* payment or billing systems;
* documents and file storage;
* scheduling tools; and
* other business systems selected by the client.

As a result, a Kitebaze workflow may process personal information relating to a client's customers, prospects, employees, contractors, suppliers, or other business contacts.

Examples may include names, email addresses, telephone numbers, appointment details, correspondence, invoices, customer records, service information, documents, and other information required for the workflow.

The exact information processed depends on the workflow being built and the systems involved.

We aim to process only the information reasonably required to make that workflow work.

#### 3. How We Use Information

We may use personal information to:

* respond to inquiries;
* provide consultations and workflow reviews;
* understand a business process or bottleneck;
* design and implement workflows;
* connect systems and applications;
* operate automations;
* configure forms, notifications, reminders, and communications;
* update records across connected systems;
* provide support and maintenance;
* troubleshoot problems;
* manage our relationship with clients;
* process payments and administer contracts;
* improve the reliability and quality of our services;
* maintain the security of our systems;
* prevent misuse, fraud, or unauthorized activity;
* meet legal, regulatory, tax, and accounting requirements; and
* communicate with you about Kitebaze where permitted by law.

We will not intentionally use personal information for purposes that are materially different from those for which it was collected without an appropriate legal basis or, where required, additional consent.

#### 4. Connected Tools and Third-Party Services

Kitebaze does not require every client to replace the software they already use.

Our work frequently involves connecting or configuring third-party products selected by us or by the client.

These may include hosting providers, cloud platforms, email systems, automation tools, CRM platforms, accounting software, communications services, analytics providers, form tools, databases, and other business applications.

When a workflow requires information to move between those services, information may be transmitted to or processed by the relevant providers.

Each third-party provider may also process information according to its own terms, privacy policy, and contractual relationship with Kitebaze or the client.

We evaluate the systems involved in each engagement and aim to limit access and data movement to what is reasonably required for the workflow.

#### 5. AI and Automated Processing

Some Kitebaze workflows may use artificial intelligence or machine-learning services when those tools are appropriate for the work being performed.

For example, this may include helping a workflow interpret documents, categorize information, extract information from text, prepare draft content, route requests, or process unstructured business information.

Where an external AI service is used, information needed to perform that task may be transmitted to the relevant provider.

The use of AI depends on the particular workflow. Kitebaze does not assume that every process requires AI and may instead use conventional automation or integrations where they are more appropriate.

We design workflows so that decisions, exceptions, approvals, or judgment that should remain with a person can remain under human control.

#### 6. Client Responsibilities

Clients are responsible for ensuring that they have the appropriate authority, consent, or other lawful basis to provide Kitebaze with access to personal information used in their workflows.

Clients are also responsible for determining which employees, contractors, systems, and information Kitebaze should be permitted to access.

Where Kitebaze processes personal information on behalf of a client, we use that information to provide the agreed services and according to the applicable agreement with that client.

#### 7. How We Share Information

We may disclose personal information to service providers where reasonably necessary to operate Kitebaze or provide our services.

These may include providers that assist with:

* cloud hosting;
* databases and storage;
* automation infrastructure;
* communications;
* analytics;
* payment processing;
* accounting;
* customer support;
* security;
* artificial intelligence services; and
* other technology required for a client's workflow.

We may also disclose information:

* where you or the relevant client directs us to;
* where necessary to complete a requested service;
* to professional advisers such as lawyers, accountants, or insurers;
* where required by law, regulation, subpoena, court order, or other lawful process;
* where reasonably necessary to protect Kitebaze, our clients, users, or others from fraud, misuse, security threats, or harm; or
* in connection with a merger, acquisition, financing, restructuring, sale, or transfer of all or part of our business.

Kitebaze does not sell personal information as part of our business model.

#### 8. International Processing and Data Location

Kitebaze is based in Canada, but some of the technology providers used by Kitebaze or our clients may operate infrastructure in other countries.

As a result, personal information may be transferred to, stored in, or processed in jurisdictions outside your province or outside Canada.

Information processed in another jurisdiction may be subject to the laws of that jurisdiction.

Where appropriate, we consider data location, security, contractual protections, and the nature of the information when selecting or configuring providers.

#### 9. Security

We use reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards appropriate to the nature of the information we handle.

These may include measures such as:

* access controls;
* authentication;
* limiting access to people who require it;
* encrypted connections;
* secure cloud infrastructure;
* system permissions;
* credential management;
* monitoring and logging;
* backups where appropriate; and
* limiting the information collected or retained.

No internet-based system or method of electronic storage can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

Clients should not provide Kitebaze with access to information that is unnecessary for the agreed workflow.

#### 10. Data Retention

We retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, to provide our services, to meet contractual obligations, or to satisfy legal, accounting, security, or regulatory requirements.

Retention periods may vary depending on:

* the type of information;
* the client engagement;
* the system in which the information is stored;
* contractual requirements;
* legal requirements; and
* whether the information is required for security, dispute resolution, or recordkeeping.

When information is no longer reasonably required, we may delete, anonymize, or securely dispose of it.

Information contained in a client's own systems may remain subject to that client's retention policies even after Kitebaze's engagement ends.

#### 11. Cookies and Analytics

Our website may use cookies and similar technologies to operate properly, remember preferences, measure website performance, and understand how visitors use the site.

You may be able to control or disable cookies through your browser.

Disabling certain cookies may affect how parts of the website function.

Where required by applicable law, we will request consent before using non-essential cookies or similar technologies.

#### 12. Marketing Communications

If you request information from us, become a client, or otherwise provide appropriate consent, we may send you communications about Kitebaze services, updates, or related information.

We comply with applicable requirements governing commercial electronic communications.

You can unsubscribe from promotional emails using the unsubscribe option included in the message or by contacting us.

We may still send communications that are necessary to provide services, administer an account, respond to a request, or manage an existing client relationship.

#### 13. Access, Correction and Privacy Requests

Depending on applicable law and the circumstances, you may have rights relating to personal information about you, including the ability to:

* request access to your personal information;
* ask us to correct inaccurate information;
* withdraw consent where processing is based on consent;
* ask questions about how your information is used or disclosed; or
* request deletion of certain information where applicable.

Some requests may be limited where we are legally or contractually required to retain information.

If the information is being processed by Kitebaze on behalf of one of our clients, we may direct your request to that client because they control the underlying business relationship and information.

We may need to verify your identity before completing a privacy request.

#### 14. Children's Privacy

Kitebaze's website and services are designed for businesses and are not directed to children.

We do not knowingly collect personal information directly from children through our website for the purpose of offering Kitebaze services to them.

If a client's workflow involves information relating to minors, the client is responsible for ensuring that the information can lawfully be provided and processed.

#### 15. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy as Kitebaze, our services, our technology, or applicable requirements change.

When we make changes, we will update the “Last updated” date at the top of this page.

If a change materially affects how we handle personal information, we may provide additional notice where appropriate.

#### 16. Contact Us

Questions, requests, or concerns about this Privacy Policy or Kitebaze's handling of personal information can be directed to:

**Kitebaze**
Website: **kitebaze.com**
Email: **[privacy@kitebaze.com](mailto:privacy@kitebaze.com)**

If your concern relates to information Kitebaze processes for one of our clients, please identify the relevant business or service when contacting us so we can determine the appropriate way to handle your request.

The website is operated by **Kitebaze** (“Kitebaze,” “we,” “us,” or “our”).

Kitebaze helps businesses improve how work gets done.

We identify operational bottlenecks, redesign workflows, connect existing software, automate repetitive work, and build systems around the way a business actually operates.

#### 2. Website Use

#### 6. Information You Submit

### Vulnerability Disclosure Policy

**Last updated: September 24, 2026**

Kitebaze takes the security of our website, systems, and client solutions seriously.

If you believe you have discovered a security vulnerability in a system operated by Kitebaze, we appreciate responsible disclosure so we can investigate and address the issue.

This Vulnerability Disclosure Policy explains how to report security issues and the rules that apply when conducting security research involving Kitebaze systems.

#### 1. Our Expectations

When investigating or reporting a potential vulnerability, please:

* **Act in good faith.** Test only to the extent necessary to identify and demonstrate the issue.
* **Respect privacy.** Do not access, modify, download, delete, or expose information belonging to another person or business.
* **Avoid disruption.** Do not interfere with the availability or normal operation of our website, systems, or services.
* **Do not exploit vulnerabilities beyond what is necessary to demonstrate them.**
* **Report vulnerabilities promptly.**
* **Keep vulnerability details confidential** until Kitebaze has had a reasonable opportunity to investigate and address the issue.

If you encounter sensitive information while testing, stop testing and notify us.

#### 2. Scope

This policy applies only to systems that are owned, operated, or directly controlled by Kitebaze.

This may include:

* **kitebaze.com**;
* Kitebaze-operated web applications;
* public-facing tools or demonstrations operated by Kitebaze;
* APIs or endpoints operated directly by Kitebaze; and
* infrastructure that Kitebaze explicitly identifies as being within scope.

If you are unsure whether a system is operated by Kitebaze, contact us before testing it.

#### 3. Client and Third-Party Systems

Kitebaze builds workflows around software and systems used by our clients.

Those systems may be operated by third parties such as cloud providers, CRM platforms, email providers, automation tools, AI providers, accounting systems, communications platforms, or other software vendors.

**This policy does not authorize security testing of:**

* systems owned or operated by a Kitebaze client;
* client websites, accounts, databases, or infrastructure;
* third-party products or platforms integrated with a Kitebaze workflow;
* services provided by external vendors; or
* systems that Kitebaze does not directly control.

The fact that a third-party system is connected to, linked from, or used by Kitebaze does not give permission to test that system.

Security issues involving a third-party service should generally be reported to that provider under its own vulnerability-disclosure process.

If you discover an issue in a Kitebaze implementation that you believe exposes a client or third-party system, please report the issue to Kitebaze without attempting further access.

#### 4. Prohibited Testing

The following activities are not permitted under this policy:

* denial-of-service or distributed denial-of-service attacks;
* attempts to overwhelm systems with traffic or requests;
* destructive testing;
* deleting, modifying, or corrupting information;
* accessing another person's account or information;
* downloading or extracting information that is not your own;
* social engineering, phishing, or impersonation;
* testing employees, contractors, clients, or suppliers without permission;
* physical security testing;
* malware deployment;
* ransomware or extortion;
* credential stuffing or testing credentials obtained from third-party breaches;
* attempts to obtain passwords, authentication tokens, or other credentials belonging to another person;
* intentionally maintaining persistent access to Kitebaze systems; or
* any activity that violates applicable law.

Automated vulnerability scanning that creates excessive traffic, disruption, or risk is also prohibited unless Kitebaze has provided prior written authorization.

#### 5. What to Report

We are particularly interested in vulnerabilities that could reasonably affect the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of Kitebaze systems or information.

Examples may include:

* authentication or authorization vulnerabilities;
* unauthorized access to accounts or information;
* exposure of sensitive information;
* injection vulnerabilities;
* serious cross-site scripting vulnerabilities;
* insecure API endpoints;
* privilege escalation;
* security configuration issues that create a meaningful risk;
* vulnerabilities that allow unauthorized actions to be performed; and
* weaknesses that could compromise Kitebaze-controlled infrastructure.

Please avoid submitting purely theoretical issues that cannot reasonably be exploited.

#### 6. Vulnerabilities Generally Not Considered Security Issues

Unless they create a meaningful security impact, the following may not require action:

* missing security headers without an exploitable vulnerability;
* low-impact clickjacking;
* self-XSS;
* issues requiring physical access to a user's device;
* vulnerabilities that exist only in obsolete browsers or unsupported software;
* software-version disclosure;
* rate-limiting observations that do not create a meaningful security risk;
* DNS or email configuration recommendations without a demonstrated impact;
* automated scanner results without validation;
* general security-hardening suggestions; and
* reports based only on publicly available information.

We may still review these reports, but they may not be treated as vulnerabilities.

#### 7. How to Report a Vulnerability

Please send suspected security vulnerabilities to:

**[security@kitebaze.com](mailto:security@kitebaze.com)**

Your report should include, where possible:

* a description of the vulnerability;
* the affected URL, endpoint, or system;
* steps required to reproduce the issue;
* screenshots, logs, or other supporting evidence;
* the potential security impact;
* any relevant technical details; and
* your contact information if you would like us to respond.

Please do not include unnecessary personal information or sensitive data belonging to other people in your report.

#### 8. What Happens After You Report

Kitebaze will review reports submitted under this policy and determine whether the issue affects a system within scope.

Where appropriate, we may:

* acknowledge the report;
* request additional information;
* reproduce and assess the issue;
* take steps to reduce or eliminate the vulnerability; and
* inform you when the issue has been addressed.

We cannot guarantee a particular resolution time because vulnerabilities can vary significantly in complexity, risk, and dependency on third-party systems.

#### 9. Safe Harbor

Kitebaze supports good-faith security research conducted in accordance with this policy.

If you:

* act in good faith;
* stay within the scope of this policy;
* avoid accessing or harming other people's information;
* do not disrupt our systems;
* do not exploit a vulnerability beyond what is reasonably necessary to demonstrate it; and
* promptly report the vulnerability to us,

Kitebaze will not initiate legal action against you solely for that research.

This safe harbor does not apply to conduct that is unlawful, destructive, extortionate, intentionally harmful, or outside the scope of this policy.

If you are uncertain whether a proposed action is permitted, contact us before proceeding.

#### 10. Rewards

Kitebaze does not currently operate a bug-bounty or vulnerability-reward program.

Submitting a vulnerability does not create an entitlement to payment, compensation, employment, or other reward.

If we introduce a formal reward program in the future, its terms will be published separately.

#### 11. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Vulnerability Disclosure Policy as Kitebaze's systems, services, and security practices evolve.

The current version will be published with an updated “Last updated” date.

#### 12. Contact

Security vulnerabilities should be reported to:

**Kitebaze**
Website: **kitebaze.com**
Email: **[security@kitebaze.com](mailto:security@kitebaze.com)**
